thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 streaming latency > 2.5s for service=model-stream-v2 in us-west-2. Request error rate +9% and timeouts +3%. Automated check: ECC correctable errors increasing on accelerator gpu-14. Paging oncall.
oncall-anna: acknowledging. Paging eng-sre, infra, runtime. Assigning priority P1. @eng-sre-bob you oncall? :rotating_light:
eng-sre-bob: I’m on it, joining. Can someone drop the immediate p95/p99 numbers and a brief customer-impact summary?
perf-carlos: p95 crossed 600ms -> 1.1s, p99 jumped from 1.8s -> 3.2s for the last 10m on streaming endpoints. Streaming stalls visible — tail requests are stalling at KV fetch stage. Throughput broadly unchanged but tail latency spike is ~12% of sessions hitting >2s. Impacted: streaming generate and chat streaming.
eng-sre-bob: checking node telemetry. Seeing ECC correctable counters on node node-usw2-acc-14 ramping. Also GPU temp on that board creeping 5-10C above baseline. Running quick probe:
eng-sre-bob: ```
# nvidia-smi -q -d ECC,THERMAL -i 14
GPU 14:
    ECC Errors
        Volatile
            single_bit: 128
            double_bit: 0
    Temperature
        GPU Current Temp : 91 C
        GPU Slowdown Temp : 93 C
```
infra-dana: that temp is high. Could be thermal throttling + ECC retries causing stalls. We should cordon+drain that host and fail traffic to other nodes. I'll prep drain. ETA 2-3m for drain.
oncall-anna: agreed. Priority: isolate node first to stop regressing more requests. @runtime-erin can we route streaming sessions away from gpu-14 and enable model-variant fallback (smaller quantized variant) for new sessions?
runtime-erin: yes. Pushing routing rule now: weight 0 for node-usw2-acc-14, fallback to model-stream-v2-q4f for new requests, enable aggressive KV prefix caching for the cluster. Making change in control-plane: `redwood route set --node node-usw2-acc-14 --weight 0` then `redwood rollout set model-stream-v2 --fallback model-stream-v2-q4f --grace 30s`
se-frank: I'll prep a short customer note for affected customers (only a subset of streaming sessions). Notifying enterprise contacts on current impact and mitigation.
support-grace: draft for customers:
support-grace: "We're investigating intermittent streaming tail latency affecting some chat/streaming sessions in us-west-2. We have isolated a degraded accelerator and are routing traffic to unaffected capacity. Expect reduced incidence within 15-30 minutes. We'll follow up with root cause and postmortem." Share if that's ok.
oncall-anna: good. eng-sre-bob, how critical is full node reboot vs driver reset?
eng-sre-bob: ECC correctable counts suggest hardware instability. Driver reset might clear for a short while but temp is high -> could reoccur. Plan: drain, cordon, soft-reboot GPU driver, if fails then full host reboot. Infra will prepare replacement capacity.
infra-dana: replacement nodes standing by. Kicking off drain now. Command run:
infra-dana: ```
kubectl annotate node node-usw2-acc-14 maintenance=evacuate && kubectl drain node-usw2-acc-14 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=10m
```
eng-sre-bob: seeing pods migrate off. Runtime change applied: new sessions hitting fallback model-stream-v2-q4f. Early signal: p99 coming down from 3.2s -> 1.6s in the last 45s.
perf-carlos: tail stalls reduced but some streaming sessions still see stalls at KV read stage. p95 now ~520ms, p99 ~1.2s. Error rate trending down.
runtime-erin: we also enabled aggressive KV cache TTL for 5m and prefix caching for hot keys. That should cut repeated prefix fetches causing stalls.
eng-sre-bob: after driver restart on the node (soft reset) ECC counts still increasing. Infra recommend full host reboot.
infra-dana: performing host reboot now. ETA ~4m for node to come back healthy or we'll reprovision. Reprovision path ready.
eng-sre-bob: creating incident ticket: INC-4590056789. Assigning owner: eng-sre-bob. Postmortem owner TBD after stabilization.
oncall-anna: confirm we have mitigations in place: traffic reroute ✅, KV caching ✅, node drained ✅, customer notice sent ✅. Any remaining customer-impacting paths?
support-grace: monitoring customer tickets; 3 open support threads but no escalations to SE yet. I'll keep updates in customer thread.
perf-carlos: monitoring metrics: look at this snapshot: p95 history (10m buckets) [120ms, 140ms, 520ms, 620ms, 520ms], p99 history [350ms, 400ms, 1.8s, 3.2s, 1.2s]. Good downward trend.
runtime-erin: we temporarily lowered concurrency on fallback variant to reduce tail memory pressure. That helped reduce spikes on cold KV reads.
infra-dana: node reboot complete. Post-reboot nvidia-smi shows temps back to ~62 C and ECC counts stable. Deciding to leave node cordoned for deeper hardware diagnostics.
eng-sre-bob: reintroducing node only after full hardware check. For now keep cordoned and reprovision replacement capacity to maintain buffer.
oncall-anna: final status: mitigation successful, variance reduced to baseline. p99 trending back to expected around 600-800ms for streaming. No customer SLA breaches yet but incident declared for RCA due to ECC+thermal hardware degradation. Postmortem owner: eng-sre-bob. Timeline: document events, mitigation steps, and hardware replacement plan. Linking INC ticket: INC-4590056789. Closing paging; handing off to eng-sre for postmortem follow-up.
eng-sre-bob: taking postmortem. Will include kernel/driver versions, ECC logs, room-temp correlation, and plan to replace GPU board. ETA initial draft 48h.
oncall-anna: thanks everyone. If anything regresses, re-open thread. :pray:
support-grace: customer update sent: "Mitigation complete. We have isolated a degraded accelerator and routed traffic to unaffected capacity. We're conducting hardware diagnostics and will share a postmortem." 
eng-sre-bob: marking incident as mitigated in the ticket. Will add action items: hardware replacement, automation for auto-drain on ECC spike, and improved telemetry alert thresholds for combined ECC+temp signals.
oncall-anna: handing oncall to next shift. Thread archived for postmortem details.
